verses.text: Isn't life on earth hard work for everyone? Aren't our days like the days of a hired worker?
Like a slave who longs for the evening shade, like a worker waiting for his pay,
I have been given months of misery and long nights of suffering.
When I lie down, I think, 'When will I get up? When will the night be over?' I toss and turn until dawn.
My body is covered with worms and scabs. My skin is cracked and oozing.
My days go by faster than a weaver's shuttle, and they come to an end without hope.
Remember, God, that my life is only a breath. I will never see happiness again.
Those who see me now will not see me again. You will look for me, but I will be gone.
As a cloud fades away and is gone, so a person who goes down to the grave does not come back up.
He will never come home again, and his own house will not know him any more.
So I will not keep quiet. I will speak out of the pain in my spirit. I will complain out of the bitterness in my soul.
Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that you must put a guard over me?
When I think, 'My bed will comfort me, and my couch will ease my complaint,'
then you frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions.
I would rather be strangled. I would rather die than live in this body.
I hate my life. I do not want to live forever. Leave me alone, because my days are only a breath.
What are people that you make so much of them, that you pay so much attention to them?
You check on them every morning and test them every moment.
Will you never look away from me? Won't you leave me alone even long enough to swallow?
If I have sinned, what have I done to you, you who watch over people? Why have you made me your target? Why have I become a burden to you?
Why don't you forgive my wrongs and take away my sins? Soon I will lie down in the dust. You will search for me, but I will be gone."
